scope: A disposable Kubernetes v1.36.1 Kind cluster reconciles native Prometheus Operator Prometheus, ServiceMonitor, and PodMonitor resources. Namespace-scoped discovery RBAC and selector labels limit scraping to two safe synthetic CPU workload endpoints. Prometheus queries verify no samples before enrollment and bounded training-stage, measured latency, and quality markers from the original synthetic workloads after enrollment. A pinned llama.cpp b9519 CPU server exposes its native Prometheus metrics; the observed generation-token counter increase matches one fixed four-token completion. A pinned PyTorch 2.15.0+cpu training Job performs three optimizer steps on fixed synthetic data; Prometheus scrapes its app-owned optimizer-step counter and measured loss gauge, matched to an independent training receipt. The case also observes retirement of the two synthetic monitor targets and their instant-query series under a 30-second lookback while the llama.cpp target remains available. The reference records the selected CPU producer-to-scrape paths and fixture lifecycle. GPU/DCGM and other hardware telemetry, provider-deployed framework instrumentation, production attribution, default query lookback, and durable retention require separate evidence.

checks.claim: Before monitor enrollment healthy fixture workloads have no scrape targets or samples
The native monitors expose exact training progress, measured timings, and labeled model quality
ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor produce separate scrapes and leave the healthy unselected fixture out
The scraping identity is scoped to discovery in the fixture namespace
Prometheus observes the bounded native llama.cpp generation counter increase
Removing the training monitor retires its target and 30s-lookback series while inference and native llama remain available
Removing the inference monitor retires its target and 30s-lookback series while native llama remains available
The real PyTorch workload exposes a zero optimizer-step baseline before training
Prometheus scrapes step count and measured loss from a real pinned PyTorch CPU training run
